🛢💵 Oil prices surge to $100 amid intensified Houthi retaliation
Global crude benchmarks Brent and WTI have approached the $100-per-barrel mark after Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco’s oil facilities near the Yemen border on Monday brought production to a halt.
The strikes targeted the industrial city of Jazan, where refineries previously produced upwards of 400,000 barrels per day, in what the Houthis described as retaliation for the Saudi blockade of Yemen’s ports and airports.
In recent months, the Houthis have significantly intensified their retaliation campaign against Saudi Arabia, including:
🌏 Targeting Saudi Aramco oil refineries and energy facilities
🌏 Imposing a maritime embargo on Saudi vessels in the Red Sea
🌏 Intensifying strikes on military and aviation infrastructure, including Abha airport and King Khalid Air Base
The unfolding conflict with the Houthis adds to Saudi Arabia's long list of problems triggered by the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, during which Saudis decided to ally with the US-Israeli aggressors.
